facts: Mobileye reported Q2 2026 revenue of $508 million versus $506 million in Q2 2025, while first-half 2026 revenue was $1.066 billion versus $944 million in the first half of 2025.
The company raised and narrowed full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.970 billion-$2.020 billion, implying 4%-7% year-over-year growth.
Mobileye generated $210 million of net cash from operating activities in the six months ended June 27, 2026 and reported $1.4 billion of cash, cash equivalents, marketable securities and deposits.
Q2 EyeQ and SuperVision average system price was $48.5, down from $49.7 in Q2 2025; the company disclosed the change was partly related to product/customer mix including China OEM exposure.
Mobileye said MOIA public user testing in Hamburg with safety drivers had begun and described preparations for commercial robotaxi services as on track.

The company stated that the large improvement in its updated operating-income outlook was primarily attributable to an Israeli R&D incentive grant, so the headline margin revision is not purely operating-volume evidence.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: First-half revenue grew and operating cash flow was positive while Q2 revenue itself was approximately flat year over year.

factors.name: catalystScore
factors.basis: Late-2026/2027 advanced-product launches and robotaxi testing create identifiable commercialization milestones, but they remain execution-dependent.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Reported average EyeQ/SuperVision system price declined year over year, so current primary evidence does not support an unqualified pricing-power claim.

factors.name: executionMonitoring
factors.basis: Revenue guidance improved and MOIA testing advanced, while operating-income guidance benefited materially from an incentive grant that should be separated from underlying execution.

risks: Q2 revenue was approximately flat year over year despite stronger first-half growth.
Average system price declined year over year, creating mix/pricing uncertainty.
A material portion of the operating-income guidance improvement came from an R&D incentive grant rather than underlying unit economics.
Robotaxi and physical-AI expansion add commercialization and capital-allocation complexity beyond the established ADAS business.
contradictions: Headline operating-income guidance improvement can appear to signal sharply stronger underlying operations, but Mobileye explicitly attributes most of the revision to the R&D incentive grant; Alpha should separate that accounting/incentive effect from operating execution.
unknowns: The source does not provide a current market-price or enterprise-value input, so marketValuationOpportunity remains for Alpha to source and calculate.
The durability of lower average system price and the contribution of mix versus negotiated pricing are not fully quantified in this release.
Commercial economics and capital requirements of Mobileye's vertically integrated robotaxi initiative remain insufficiently quantified for numeric underwriting from this source alone.
